public_rationale: On the plain reading, the claim says OpenAI could not make its models cheaper at the time of the post. OpenAI's own announcements that month say otherwise. On April 14, 2025, it said that 'through efficiency improvements to our inference systems' GPT-4.1 was 26% cheaper than GPT-4o for median queries. On April 16 it said o3 and o4-mini improved cost-performance over o1 and o3-mini. If the claim instead meant OpenAI could not shrink its total spending ('footprint'), these sources do not settle that. Rising total spending would also not prove inability. The result depends on the unit-cost reading, which is flagged.
limitations: Relies on OpenAI's own statements about efficiency. Its internal costs are not disclosed.
A price cut can reflect pricing strategy as well as cost. OpenAI explicitly tied this one to efficiency.
The aggregate-spending reading is not tested.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI cannot reduce its costs at this point.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI cannot "make things cheaper" at this point, because the money has always been there to make things more expensive, as has the compute to make larger language models that burn billions of dollars a year.
statement.document_title: OpenAI Is A Systemic Risk To The Tech Industry

our_interpretation: Plain reading: at the time of the post, OpenAI was unable to make its products cheaper to run or offer, that is, to cut the cost per unit of model use through efficiency.
'At this point' fixes the claim at the time of the post. The target period is April 2025, the month of the post. This is my choice, flagged as an ambiguity.
An alternative reading is aggregate spending ('reduce its footprint'). Rising total spending would fit that reading, but it would not show inability, because higher spending can be a choice to grow.
OpenAI's own statements of efficiency-driven cost and price cuts during the period count as evidence on the plain reading.
criteria.support_condition: In April 2025 OpenAI showed no ability to lower the cost or price of serving its models. For example, new models cost more per query and there were no efficiency gains.
criteria.contradiction_condition: In April 2025 OpenAI released models or changes that were cheaper per query through efficiency improvements.
